content: Elagolix can reduce the levels or effects of etravirine by influencing the metabolism of the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer, so close monitoring of CYP3A substrates is recommended when co-administered. Dose adjustments of CYP3A substrates may be necessary. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of elbasvir/grazoprevir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided as it may reduce the therapeutic efficacy of elbasvir/grazoprevir. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of eletriptan via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of eliglustat by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Etravirine and elivaldogene autotemcel may mutually reduce each other's effects. Patients should avoid antiretroviral medications for at least one month before initiating stem cell mobilization therapy and until all apheresis cycles are completed. Etravirine increases the levels or effects of elvitegravir by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration with CYP3A inducers may decrease plasma concentrations of elvitegravir and associated protease inhibitors, leading to therapeutic failure and potential resistance. This combination is contraindicated. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of encorafenib by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided due to the potential for reduced therapeutic efficacy. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of entrectinib via CYP3A4 metabolism. Alternative therapies are recommended. Etravirine and enzalutamide mutually reduce each other's levels or effects by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative therapies considered. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of eplerenone via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of erdafitinib via CYP3A4 metabolism but increases its levels via CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Co-administration is not recommended. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of ergotamine and ergonovine via CYP3A4 metabolism. These combinations are contraindicated. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of erlotinib via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of erythromycin (base, ethylsuccinate, lactobionate, and stearate forms) via CYP3A4 metabolism, while erythromycin increases etravirine levels. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative therapies considered. Etravirine increases escitalopram levels via CYP2C19 metabolism but decreases its levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of eslicarbazepine acetate via CYP3A4 metabolism, while eslicarbazepine increases etravirine levels via CYP2C19 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Etravirine increases esomeprazole levels via CYP2C19 metabolism, and esomeprazole increases etravirine levels. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of estradiol (oral and vaginal forms), conjugated synthetic estrogens, esterified estrogens, and estropipate via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of ethinylestradiol via CYP3A4 metabolism, potentially reducing the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives. Non-hormonal contraceptive methods are recommended. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of ethosuximide via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Etravirine increases the levels or effects of ethotoin via CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of etonogestrel and etoposide via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of eucalyptus via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of everolimus via CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of exemestane via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Fedratinib increases etravirine levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism, while etravirine reduces fedratinib levels. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative therapies considered. Felbamate increases etravirine levels via CYP2C19 and CYP2C9/10 metabolism, while etravirine reduces felbamate levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Felodipine increases etravirine levels via CYP2C19 metabolism, while etravirine reduces felodipine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of fentanyl (all forms) via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration may lead to reduced efficacy or withdrawal symptoms in dependent patients. After discontinuing CYP3A4 inducers, fentanyl plasma concentrations may increase, potentially causing prolonged therapeutic or adverse effects. Alternative therapies are recommended. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of fesoterodine via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Fexinidazole increases etravirine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while etravirine increases fexinidazole levels. Co-administration is not recommended due to the risk of adverse effects. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of finasteride via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Etravirine decreases the levels or effects of finerenone via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative therapies considered. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of flibanserin via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Fluconazole increases etravirine levels via CYP2C19, CYP2C9/10, and CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Fludrocortisone reduces etravirine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while etravirine reduces fludrocortisone levels. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Fluoxetine increases etravirine levels via CYP2C9/10 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Etravirine reduces the levels or effects of flurazepam via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Etravirine increases flurbiprofen and fluvastatin levels via CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of these interactions is unknown. Fluvoxamine increases etravirine levels via CYP2C19 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative therapies considered. Etravirine increases fosamprenavir levels by reducing its metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Fosaprepitant increases etravirine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while etravirine reduces fosaprepitant levels. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Etravirine increases fosphenytoin levels via CYP2C9/10 metabolism, while fosphenytoin reduces etravirine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Etravirine reduces fostamatinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided or alternative therapies considered. Etravirine decreases fruquintinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. If co-administration is unavoidable, fruquintinib should be continued at the recommended dosage. Etravirine reduces ganaxolone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided. If unavoidable, consider increasing the ganaxolone dose without exceeding the maximum daily dose. Etravirine decreases gefitinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Gefitinib dosage may need to be increased to 500 mg daily when co-administered with strong CYP3A4 inducers. The dose should be reduced to 250 mg/day seven days after discontinuing the inducer. Etravirine reduces glasdegib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided. Etravirine decreases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels via CYP3A4 metabolism but increases their levels via P-glycoprotein inhibition. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Grapefruit increases etravirine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Griseofulvin reduces etravirine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Etravirine decreases guanfacine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. For ADHD patients, doubling the guanfacine dose may be considered. For hypertension, more frequent dosing of the immediate-release product may be required. Etravirine reduces haloperidol levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Etravirine decreases hydrocodone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Discontinuing CYP3A4 inducers may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially causing fatal respiratory depression. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Hydrocortisone reduces etravirine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while etravirine reduces hydrocortisone levels. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Etravirine decreases hydroxyprogesterone caproate levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Etravirine reduces ibrutinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided as strong CYP3A inducers decrease ibrutinib plasma concentrations by approximately tenfold. Etravirine increases ibuprofen levels via CYP2C9/10 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Etravirine decreases idelalisib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while idelalisib increases etravirine levels. Co-administration is not recommended. Etravirine increases ifosfamide toxicity by enhancing its metabolism to active alkylating metabolites and neurotoxic/nephrotoxic metabolites. Close monitoring for toxicities and dose adjustments are recommended. Etravirine reduces iloperidone levels via CYP3A4 metabolism, while iloperidone increases etravirine levels. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Imatinib increases etravirine levels via CYP2C9/10 metabolism, while etravirine reduces imatinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Etravirine increases imipramine levels via CYP2C19 metabolism but decreases its levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Etravirine reduces indinavir levels by increasing its metabolism. Co-administration is contraindicated unless indinavir is boosted with low-dose ritonavir. Etravirine decreases infigratinib levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided. Etravirine reduces irinotecan levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided. Etravirine decreases isavuconazonium sulfate levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Isoniazid increases etravirine levels via CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided. Etravirine reduces isosorbide dinitrate and mononitrate levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and close monitoring are recommended. Etravirine decreases isradipine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unknown. Istradefylline increases etravirine levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided.
